style: Say warmly with a gravelly voice, like an old park ranger telling stories
lines: The phone is ringing! Tap Answer.
Before we talk, three phone rules: listen, one group at a time, and wait your turn. The phone goes around the tables.
Oh no, the phone crackled! Which part did you miss? Say your question, then tap the card: Who, What, Where, When, Why or How.
The phone is still crackly. Ask me a question about the part you missed!
Don't know a word? Tap What does it mean?
Wait for the crackly part, then ask!
Now ask me more about it. Tap a card to hear it, then tap it again to ask.
Tap Ask it, or tap another card.
My turn to ask! Tap a picture to hear it, then tap This one.
Tap This one to choose that picture, or tap another picture.
Yes! You were listening.
Not quite. Think back to what I said.
Let's take a message. Tell the call out loud, then tap the pictures in order.
Tap the next picture in order, or tap Read the message when all four boxes are full.
Tap Read the message to check your order.
Some pictures are out of order. Look at the rings.
Fill every box first.
Thanks, class! Great listening. Bye for now!
Tap Next call for another call from Ranger Sam, or open Calls.

Hello, class! This is Ranger Sam at Pine Hollow Park. Something blew away this morning. It was a...
Hello, class! This is Ranger Sam at Pine Hollow Park. Something blew away this morning. It was a kite!
What? A kite! A red kite with a long tail.
A girl named Mia was flying it by the pond. Then the wind pulled it right out of her hands.
Now it's stuck way up...
Now it's stuck way up in the tallest pine tree.
Where? In the tallest pine tree in the park!
But don't worry... came to help.
But don't worry. The fire crew came to help.
Who? The fire crew, with their tall ladder!
A crew is a team of people who work together.
Did Mia get her kite back?
She did! It has a little rip, but it still flies.
What's your favorite color?
Ha! Let's stay on the kite.
What blew away?
A kite
A hat
A balloon
Where did it get stuck?
In the pine tree
On a roof
In the pond
Kite flying by the pond
Wind pulls it away
Kite stuck in the tree
Fire crew with a ladder
Message: Mia was flying her kite by the pond. The wind pulled it away. The kite got stuck in the tallest pine tree. The fire crew came with a tall ladder to help.
Hello, class! Ranger Sam here. We have big news at the park farm. A baby goat was born...
Hello, class! Ranger Sam here. We have big news at the park farm. A baby goat was born last night!
When? Last night, just before midnight!
A baby goat is called a kid. Her mother's name is Clover.
The kid is tiny, and she can already...
The kid is tiny, and she can already stand up and walk.
What can she do? She can stand up and walk!
She needs a name. We will choose it...
She needs a name. We will choose it by a vote.
How? The children who visit will vote!
A kid is a baby goat. People call children kids too!
What does the baby goat look like?
She's white, with one brown ear.
Do you have a big red bike at home?
Ha! Let's stay on the baby goat.
When was she born?
At night
In the morning
At lunch
How will they choose her name?
A vote
Names in a hat
Clover picks
Clover the goat in the barn
Baby goat born at night
The kid stands and walks
Children vote on a name
Message: Clover the mother goat was in the barn. Her baby goat was born last night. The little kid can already stand and walk. Children who visit will vote on her name.
Hello, class! It's Ranger Sam. I had to stop my truck today. A... was crossing the road!
Hello, class! It's Ranger Sam. I had to stop my truck today. A turtle was crossing the road!
What? A turtle! A little box turtle.
It was walking very slowly toward the pond, its habitat.
I stopped my truck...
I stopped my truck so cars would not hurt it.
Why? Because cars could hurt it, and turtles move slowly.
Then I helped it across the road...
Then I helped it across the road, carrying it gently.
How? I carried it gently, the same way it was going. If you see a turtle on a road, tell a grown-up.
A habitat is the place where an animal lives and finds its food.
Was the turtle big or small?
Small! About as big as my hand.
Can I have a snack?
Ha! Let's stay on the turtle.
Why did Ranger Sam stop?
Cars could hurt the turtle
Sam was sleepy
To eat lunch
Which way did Sam carry it?
The way it was going
Back into the woods
Into the truck
A turtle on the road
Sam stops the truck
Sam carries it gently
The turtle reaches the pond
Message: A box turtle was crossing the road. Ranger Sam stopped the truck to keep it safe. Sam carried the turtle gently the way it was going. The turtle reached the pond.
Hello, class! Ranger Sam calling. Last night we had a big storm with lots of...
Hello, class! Ranger Sam calling. Last night we had a big storm with lots of wind and rain.
What? Wind! Very strong wind, and rain.
The wind knocked a big tree down...
The wind knocked a big tree down across the Blue Trail.
Where? Right across the Blue Trail!
So the Blue Trail is closed. It will open again...
So the Blue Trail is closed. It will open again on Saturday.
When? On Saturday, after we cut the tree away.
A trail is a path through the woods.
Was anyone hurt?
Nobody was hurt. Everyone stayed safe inside.
I like pizza with lots of cheese!
Ha! Let's stay on the storm.
What knocked the tree down?
Strong wind
A bear
A truck
When will the trail open?
On Saturday
Tonight
In the winter snow
A storm with wind and rain
A tree falls on the trail
The trail is closed
Workers cut the tree away
Message: A big storm brought strong wind and rain. A tree fell right across the Blue Trail. The trail was closed to keep people safe. Workers cut the tree away so it opens Saturday.
Hello, class! Ranger Sam here. High up in a hollow tree, I found a nest of baby...
Hello, class! Ranger Sam here. High up in a hollow tree, I found a nest of baby owls!
What? Owls! Baby owls.
Baby owls are called owlets. There are three of them.
We put up a rope so people stay back...
We put up a rope so people stay back, so the owls can rest.
Why? So the owl family can rest. Many owls sleep in the day and hunt at night.
You can still see them...
You can still see them, with binoculars.
How? With binoculars, from the bench by the sign!
Owlets are baby owls.
What do the owlets look like?
Fluffy and gray, like little cotton balls with big eyes.
Is it my birthday?
Ha! Let's stay on the owls.
How many owlets are there?
Three owlets
One owlet
Five owlets
Why is there a rope?
So the owls can rest
For a running race
To fly kites
Sam finds a hollow tree
Three owlets in the nest
A rope keeps people back
People watch with binoculars
Message: Ranger Sam found a nest in a hollow tree. Three baby owlets live inside. A rope keeps people back so the owls can rest. Visitors watch them with binoculars from the bench.
Hello, class! It's Ranger Sam. This morning there was new snow, and I found tracks...
Hello, class! It's Ranger Sam. This morning there was new snow, and I found tracks by the picnic tables.
Where? All around the picnic tables!
Each track had four toes. They went in a line, one in front of the other.
Then I saw who made them. It was a...
Then I saw who made them. It was a red fox!
Who? A red fox, looking for food.
The fox was out...
The fox was out before the sun came up.
When? Very early, before the sun came up.
Tracks are the marks feet leave in snow or mud.
Did the fox find food?
It sniffed under the bird feeder, hunting for mice. Then it ran into the woods.
My shoes are new!
Ha! Let's stay on the tracks.
Who made the tracks?
A red fox
A deer
A duck
Where were the tracks?
By the picnic tables
On the cabin roof
New snow at the park
Tracks by the picnic tables
Red fox early in the morning
The fox runs into the woods
Message: New snow fell at Pine Hollow Park. Four-toed tracks went around the picnic tables. A red fox made them before the sun came up. Then the fox ran into the woods.
